prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first, what kind of project is it (full remodel, kitchen/bath, roof, HVAC, plumbing, small repairs)? That affects which contractors are best. If you want, I can then recommend likely local companies and draft messages to request bids.

Meanwhile, here are practical, reliable steps to find and vet a contractor in Joplin, MO, plus things to watch for:

Where to look
- Ask neighbors, friends, or co-workers in Joplin who recently had similar work done. Word-of-mouth is often best.
- Nextdoor and local Facebook groups (Joplin community pages) for recent personal referrals.
- Google and Yelp — sort by rating + recent reviews; read several detailed reviews, not just stars.
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints and ratings.
- Angi / HomeAdvisor /Thumbtack for pros who handle estimates and screening (use reviews as one input).
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — they can point to established local businesses.
- City of Joplin Building Division — to confirm permit requirements and if a contractor has a history of code issues.

How to vet contractors
- Get at least 3 written bids for the same scope of work so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- Ask for local references (preferably projects completed in the last 12–24 months). Call them and ask about timeliness, cleanliness, communication, changes/orders, and final cost.
- Verify trade licenses where applicable. (Missouri has state licenses for electricians, plumbers, HVAC; general contracting licensing is local—check what Joplin requires.)
- Confirm liability insurance and workers’ comp insurance. Ask for certificates naming you as “certificate holder” while work is on your property.
- Check for complaints or reviews on BBB, Google, and Facebook.
- Ask how they handle permits and inspections. Good contractors pull permits and coordinate inspections; beware those who say they’ll avoid permits.
- Review portfolio/photos of recent similar projects.

Questions to ask during the first call/estimate
- How long have you been in business in Joplin? How many similar projects have you finished recently?
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of finished jobs?
- Who will be on-site (subcontractors or employees)? Will you supervise daily?
- What’s the estimated timeline and start date? How will changes be handled?
- What is your payment schedule? (Avoid large up-front lump sums—typical: deposit, progress payments, final payment.)
- Do you provide a written contract with scope, materials, timeline, payment schedule, and warranty?
- Do you carry liability and workers’ comp insurance? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you pull permits? Who handles inspections?

Contract and payment tips
- Get everything in writing: scope, materials (brands/colors), timeline, start/end dates, cleanup, disposal, and warranty.
- Include a clear change-order process and unit pricing for likely extras.
- Do not pay full balance until final inspection, lien waivers from subs, and you’re satisfied.
- Typical red flags: large up-front cash request, no written contract, high-pressure sales, refusing to provide references or insurance proof, vague timeline.

If you want, I can:
- Help narrow good local options if you tell me the project type and your preferred budget/timeline.
- Draft a short message/email you can send to contractors to request bids.
- Create a checklist you can use during on-site estimates.

Which would you like to do next?
